title: Time-to-first-token playbook & deployment fit - Emberly Studio
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private fit
summary: Emberly Studio is evaluating Redwood for a rapid prototyping path (PLG/self-serve) with a short runway to first token for an internal proof-of-concept. They want to understand free credits, expected TTFT, and the decision factors between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Security (KMS, SSO, audit logs) and predictable latency/cost are gating items. Next steps are to send pricing & playbook and schedule a benchmarks run with sample prompts.
next_steps: Jordan Reyes: Send self-serve playbook + pricing sheet (include credits options) - due 2025-05-20
Ayesha Patel: Propose a 2-hour bench run with sample prompts and target latency SLOs - propose dates by 2025-05-22
Liam Chen: Share sample prompt set and expected QPS by 2025-05-19
action_items: Jordan Reyes: email pricing + quickstart guide (due 2025-05-20)
Ayesha Patel: schedule benchmark run and prepare runbook (due 2025-05-22)
Liam Chen: provide prompt corpus + traffic pattern (due 2025-05-19)
Marco Ruiz: provide security contact and any special compliance constraints (due 2025-05-23)
header:
Date: 2025-05-17
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Reyes (Redwood AE), Ayesha Patel (Redwood SE), Ravi Malhotra (Redwood SE?), Liam Chen (CTO, Emberly), Priya Nair (ML Eng), Marco Ruiz (Head of Infra), Alex (Product)
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Reyes: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I see Liam, Priya, Marco - hi. Quick agenda: 1) Where you are with the POC, 2) how fast you need TTFT, 3) hosted vs dedicated vs private fit, 4) security questions.
[00:27] Liam Chen: Yeah thanks. We're moving pretty fast - want to prototype a conversational assist inside our creative editor. Primary goal is time-to-first-token so the product team can demo next month. We have a small prompt set and maybe 5-10 QPS for the POC.
[00:54] Priya Nair: To add, model choice is flexible — prefer open models for cost, but we care about latency - under 300ms median would be great.
[01:12] Ayesha Patel: Cool. For TTFT with Redwood's self-serve, most teams hit first response in a few minutes if they use the SDK and the provided quickstart. Free credits can cover early testing — Jordan, can you confirm the usual credit size?
[01:30] Jordan Reyes: Yeah we usually offer 25k tokens of starter credits for PLG signups, sometimes 50k for larger evals. We'll include that in the email.
[01:45] Marco Ruiz: Important: our infra team needs to know about data residency and keys. We use AWS KMS and strict IAM. If we go private we need to keep the KV cache on our VPC, and audit logs shipped to our Splunk.
[02:10] Ravi Malhotra: (overlap) — yeah audit logs are standard. For private deployments we do customer-managed KMS integrations and can set up an audit log forwarder. For hosted, we provide exportable logs and retention settings.
[02:30] Alex (Product): On dedicated vs hosted — is dedicated just reserved capacity or also performance-tuned kernels?
[02:45] Ayesha Patel: Dedicated is a reserved GPU pool with predictable throughput and pinning, so you'll see less variance. The runtime picks kernels based on model and input length; dedicated can be configured with quantization profiles if you want to tune cost/latency tradeoffs.
[03:10] Liam Chen: If we start PLG/self-serve hosted and then move to dedicated later, how much friction?
[03:22] Jordan Reyes: Minimal. Same API surface, just change deployment flag and you can pin a model version for rollout. We handle model routing and fallback automatically. You won't need to rewrite code.
[03:40] Priya Nair: What about SSO and SAML? We want RBAC before we start sharing API keys with product folks.
[03:50] Jordan Reyes: Enterprise accounts have SSO/SAML and fine-grained RBAC. For the initial self-serve you'll get a single workspace but we can enable SSO if you choose a paid plan or during pilot onboarding.
[04:10] Marco Ruiz: Latency guarantees — hosted has soft SLOs, but for production we need contract SLAs.
[04:20] Ayesha Patel: Right. Hosted has published median latencies for verified models; Dedicated includes SLA-backed uptime and latency targets depending on the reserved tier. Private deployments can be installed behind your network with latency bounded by your infra.
[04:40] Speaker 6: Sorry, quick Q: does Redwood support prefix caching or KV cache to reduce token cost?
[04:50] Ravi Malhotra: Yes, we have automatic KV cache and prefix caching; it can be enabled by policy and reduces per-request compute. For chat workloads, continuous batching and KV cache are big cost savers.
[05:10] Liam Chen: For our prompt set (mostly short context + image metadata) caching might help. How do we benchmark cost vs latency?
[05:22] Ayesha Patel: We run a benchmark with your prompts, measure per-token latency, throughput at target QPS, and estimate unit cost under different batching/quantization configs. We can share a benchmark spreadsheet after the run.
[05:40] Priya Nair: That would be great — we want to test a 1k sample of prompts.
[05:47] Jordan Reyes: Action item: Priya to share sample prompts + traffic pattern. We'll run the bench and come back with numbers.
[06:02] Marco Ruiz: Security detail - do you support bringing your own KMS in hosted mode?
[06:10] Ravi Malhotra: For hosted, we do not typically integrate customer KMS directly; we offer encryption at rest and in transit, and allow exportable audit logs and dedicated key management for higher tiers. For Private, BYOK is supported.
[06:30] Alex (Product): Any gotchas with model variants — like when fallback kicks in and output changes? We worry about regressions in quality during failover.
[06:44] Ayesha Patel: We support rollout policies and can pin model versions to avoid silent shifts. Also Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization and model variant choices and flag quality regressions against your eval set.
[07:02] Liam Chen: Pricing basics for POC — want to know the rough per-1k-token cost and any minimums.
[07:12] Jordan Reyes: I'll send a starter pricing sheet. Hosted per-token for small open models is typically lower than closed models; we'll include ranges. No hard minimum for self-serve, but pilot SKUs for dedicated require a commit.
[07:30] Priya Nair: Is there an interactive sandbox or dashboard we can use to try models without code?
[07:38] Jordan Reyes: Yes, the Redwood console has per-route/model dashboards and a playground to run prompts. We'll send invite access with the credits.
[07:50] (crosstalk)
[08:05] Ayesha Patel: Quick technical note — if you care about sub-200ms tails, we'll want to optimize serving with continuous batching and smaller sequence lengths. For larger contexts we may suggest quantized variants to reduce CPU/GPU time.
[08:28] Marco Ruiz: For latency-sensitive parts, would you recommend Dedicated or Private?
[08:36] Ayesha Patel: Dedicated first. Private if you have strict compliance or need the model within your network. Dedicated gives the best mix of managed service with predictable latency.
[08:50] Liam Chen: Ok. Timeline for us: want POC demo in 3 weeks, production in 3 months if things look good.
[08:58] Jordan Reyes: Sounds reasonable. We'll prioritize the bench this week.
[09:05] Priya Nair: About logs retention — do you allow configuring retention per workspace?
[09:12] Ravi Malhotra: Yes, retention is configurable; for enterprise pilots we can set longer retention and forward logs to your SIEM.
[09:25] Speaker 6: Any known issues with image-augmented prompts? We may send metadata + small thumbnails.
[09:33] Ayesha Patel: Supported, but models vary — we'll recommend specific open models that handle multimodal inputs, and we'll benchmark those.
[09:45] Liam Chen: Will you run the bench in our region? We need ap-southeast-1 availability because our users are there.
[09:55] Jordan Reyes: We have hosted regions in NA and EU and are expanding to APAC; for benchmarks we can run a routed test to closer infra or replicate load to estimate. If APAC region isn't available, Dedicated or Private can be provisioned in that region via partners.
[10:18] Marco Ruiz: Security audit check: do you have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001?
[10:24] Ravi Malhotra: We are SOC 2 Type II and working on ISO. We'll share the current compliance pack and pen test summary.
[10:40] Jordan Reyes: I'll attach the security pack and an onboarding checklist in the follow-up email.
[10:50] Priya Nair: One more operational Q — how do we handle rate limits during early tests? We want to open up to product folks but not blow up the bill.
[11:00] Jordan Reyes: You can set per-token quotas and rate-limits at the API key level; the console has cost alerts. We'll show that in the playground invite.
[11:15] Liam Chen: Great. Anything else we should clarify for the bench run?
[11:22] Ayesha Patel: We'll need your prompt set, target QPS, desired latency SLOs, and if you'll enable context caching. We'll run a runbook and share the spreadsheet.
[11:35] Priya Nair: We'll provide that by Monday.
[11:40] Jordan Reyes: Cool. Recap: 1) Jordan sends credits + playbook + pricing + security pack, 2) Priya sends prompts and traffic, 3) Ayesha schedules bench.
[12:00] (background noise)
[20:05] Liam Chen: (later in meeting) can you confirm the demo flow for product folks? We want a one-button embed to call Redwood for suggestions.
[20:20] Ayesha Patel: We generally recommend a small wrapper service that controls API keys and does prefix caching; that gives you a safe integration pattern. For the POC that's optional but recommended for production.
[30:45] Marco Ruiz: We're also thinking about RBAC for model variants — can we limit which teams can call large models due to cost?
[30:58] Jordan Reyes: Yes, the console supports route-level controls and token quotas per key. You can gate expensive models behind specific roles.
[35:10] Priya Nair: Any sample runbooks for moving from self-serve to dedicated?
[35:22] Jordan Reyes: We'll include a migration playbook with checklist items: pin model, configure autoscaling policies, enable audit forwarding, and set up rollout canary.
[38:00] Liam Chen: Perfect. One last ask — can you include a simple cost estimate for our 5-10 QPS over a 2-week POC in the email?
[38:12] Jordan Reyes: Yes, we'll include a best-effort estimate and notes about batching to reduce unit costs.
[41:00] Jordan Reyes: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and links. Meeting adjourned.

Note: transcript has occasional mislabels and filler; timestamps approximate.
